department: Doctorate in Chemistry (TUM School of Natural Sciences)

deadline.value: No central deadline: apply to advertised research-associate positions or directly to a supervisor.
deadline.quote: as the doctorate is highly individualized, there is no central application platform for doctoral programs where you can submit your application documents.

supervisor.value: You must first find a supervisor among the teaching staff of the School of Natural Sciences.
supervisor.quote: The first step to starting your doctorate is to find a supervisor among the

funding.value: Most common route is a salaried research-associate position; self-initiated applicants usually need their own funding such as a scholarship. No tuition fees.
funding.quote: At TUM, the most common way to do your doctorate is within the framework of employment as research staff at your research group/chair. | self-initiated applications do not automatically imply employment at TUM that comes with a monthly salary; thus, in most cases, you must take care of your funding, e.g., with an external scholarship.

entry_route.value: An above-average master's-level degree is needed; no fast-track, so bachelor's-only admission is not possible.
entry_route.quote: Please note that TUM does not offer “fast-track doctoral programs.” Therefore, admission to a doctoral program with only a Bachelor's degree is not possible.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field: ETS discontinued the GRE Chemistry Test in May 2023.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Chemistry Test was discontinued in May 2023.

notes: Individual doctorate model; funding, entry and deadline rules are TUM Graduate School-wide. Degree awarded by the responsible TUM School.
